title: Saladin
subtitle: Sultan of Egypt and Syria
description: Saladin was a Kurdish Muslim ruler and founder of the Ayyubid dynasty. He became one of the most prominent political and military leaders of the medieval Middle East.
biography: Saladin rose to prominence during a period of intense political competition between the Fatimid Caliphate, the Zengid dynasty, the Crusader states, and other regional powers. After establishing his authority in Egypt and later Syria, he founded the Ayyubid dynasty and became one of the most powerful rulers of the medieval Islamic world.

title: Genghis Khan
subtitle: Founder of the Mongol Empire
description: Mongol ruler who united the Mongol tribes and established one of history's largest contiguous empires.

title: Alexander the Great
subtitle: Macedonian King
description: Macedonian ruler whose campaigns created one of the largest empires of the ancient world.

title: Ayyubid Sultanate
subtitle: 1171 – 1260 AD
description: A medieval Muslim dynasty founded by Saladin that ruled territories across Egypt, Syria, the Hejaz, Yemen, and parts of the Levant.
overview: The Ayyubid Sultanate was a medieval dynasty founded by Saladin after the abolition of the Fatimid Caliphate in Egypt. At its height, Ayyubid rulers controlled a large portion of Egypt, Syria, the Hejaz, Yemen, and parts of the Levant.
territory: Egypt, Syria, the Hejaz, Yemen, and parts of the Levant

title: Mongol Empire
subtitle: 1206 – 1368 AD
description: The largest contiguous land empire in history, founded by Genghis Khan and expanded across much of Eurasia.

title: Roman Empire
subtitle: 27 BC – 476 AD
description: One of the most influential empires in world history, centered on the Mediterranean and extending across Europe, North Africa, and Western Asia.

title: Battle of Hattin
subtitle: 1187 AD
description: A decisive battle in which Saladin defeated the main field army of the Kingdom of Jerusalem.

title: Battle of Gaugamela
subtitle: 331 BC
description: Alexander the Great defeated Darius III of Persia in one of the decisive battles of the ancient world.

title: Constantinople
subtitle: Byzantine Imperial Capital
description: The historic city that served as the capital of the Byzantine Empire and one of the most important cities of the medieval world.

title: Nur ad-Din Zengi
subtitle: Zengid ruler of Syria
description: A powerful Zengid ruler who played a central role in the political and military struggles of Syria and the Crusader states.

title: Shirkuh
subtitle: Zengid general and uncle of Saladin
description: A prominent Kurdish military commander who served Nur ad-Din Zengi and played a decisive role in the conquest of Egypt.

title: Damascus
subtitle: Historic Capital of Syria
description: One of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world and an important political, cultural, and religious center of the Middle East.
overview: Damascus has played a major role in the history of the Levant. During the medieval period it became an important center of Islamic political and cultural life and served as one of the principal capitals of the Ayyubid Sultanate.
significance: Damascus became one of Saladin's principal centers of power and later served as an important Ayyubid capital.

title: Jerusalem
subtitle: Historic Holy City
description: A city of extraordinary religious and political importance whose history spans thousands of years.
overview: Jerusalem has been one of the most important cities in the religious and political history of the Middle East. During the Crusades it became the center of the Kingdom of Jerusalem before being recaptured by Saladin in 1187.
significance: The capture of Jerusalem by Saladin in 1187 became one of the defining events of the Crusades.

title: Cairo
subtitle: Capital of Egypt
description: The historic Egyptian capital that became a major political and cultural center of the medieval Islamic world.
overview: Cairo became one of the most important cities of medieval Egypt. Saladin established his political authority in Egypt and later made Cairo one of the principal centers of the Ayyubid state.
significance: Cairo was the political center of Egypt during the transition from Fatimid to Ayyubid rule.

title: Aleppo
subtitle: Historic Syrian City
description: An ancient Syrian city that became an important political and commercial center of northern Syria.
overview: Aleppo was one of the most important cities of medieval northern Syria. It served as a major center under the Zengid dynasty and later became part of the Ayyubid political sphere.
significance: Aleppo was a major center of the Zengid dynasty and played an important role in the political struggles surrounding the Crusader states.

title: Hattin
subtitle: Galilee · Levant
description: A historic location near the Sea of Galilee that became famous as the site of Saladin's decisive victory over the Crusader army in 1187.
overview: Hattin became historically significant because of the major battle fought there in July 1187. Saladin's victory destroyed much of the field army of the Kingdom of Jerusalem and transformed the balance of power in the region.
significance: The Horns of Hattin became the site of one of the most important battles of the Crusades.

title: Tiberias
subtitle: Sea of Galilee
description: A historic city on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee that played an important role in the events surrounding the Battle of Hattin.
overview: Tiberias was an important settlement on the Sea of Galilee and became strategically significant during the Crusades. Its connection with the Battle of Hattin placed the city within one of the most important military campaigns of 1187.
significance: Tiberias and its surrounding region formed part of the strategic landscape of the campaign that culminated in the Battle of Hattin.

title: First Crusade
subtitle: 1096 – 1099 AD
description: A major military expedition launched by Western European Christian forces toward the eastern Mediterranean following the call for aid from the Byzantine Empire.
overview: The First Crusade was the first major Crusader expedition to the Holy Land. Crusader armies travelled across Europe and the Byzantine territories before capturing Jerusalem in 1099.
significance: The First Crusade resulted in the establishment of several Crusader states in the eastern Mediterranean, including the Kingdom of Jerusalem.

timeline.description: The main Crusader armies began their campaigns toward the eastern Mediterranean.
Crusader forces participated in the siege and capture of Nicaea.
Antioch was captured after a prolonged siege.

title: Capture of Jerusalem
subtitle: 1099 AD
description: The capture of Jerusalem by Crusader forces during the First Crusade.
overview: After a prolonged siege, Crusader forces breached the defenses of Jerusalem in July 1099 and captured the city.
significance: The capture established Jerusalem as the political and religious center of the newly formed Kingdom of Jerusalem.

timeline.description: Crusader forces arrived before Jerusalem and began preparing for the siege.
Siege equipment was constructed and the Crusader assault intensified.
Crusader forces breached the city's defenses and captured Jerusalem.

title: Recapture of Jerusalem
subtitle: 1187 AD
description: Saladin's recapture of Jerusalem following the Ayyubid victory at the Battle of Hattin.
overview: Following the decisive victory at Hattin, Saladin's forces advanced through the Kingdom of Jerusalem. The city itself was besieged and eventually surrendered in October 1187.
significance: The recapture of Jerusalem transformed the political balance of the Crusader states and became one of the defining moments of Saladin's career.

timeline.description: Saladin defeated the main Crusader field army at Hattin.
Ayyubid forces reached Jerusalem and began the siege.

title: Treaty of Jaffa
subtitle: 1192 AD
description: An agreement that brought the Third Crusade to an end and established a period of peace between Saladin and Richard the Lionheart.
overview: The Treaty of Jaffa ended the major military phase of the Third Crusade. Jerusalem remained under Muslim control while Crusaders retained territory along the coast.
significance: The agreement established a period of relative stability between the Ayyubid forces and the Crusader states.

timeline.description: Richard the Lionheart captured important coastal positions during the Third Crusade.
Negotiations between Richard and Saladin intensified.
The Treaty of Jaffa was concluded.

title: Fall of Baghdad
subtitle: 1258 AD
description: The capture and destruction of Baghdad by the Mongol forces led by Hulagu Khan.
overview: Mongol forces under Hulagu Khan captured Baghdad in 1258, bringing the Abbasid caliphate in Baghdad to an end.
significance: The fall of Baghdad became one of the major turning points in the history of the medieval Islamic world.

timeline.description: Mongol forces approached Baghdad and surrounded the city.
Baghdad's defenses collapsed and the city was captured.

title: Fall of Constantinople
subtitle: 1453 AD
description: The Ottoman conquest of Constantinople under Sultan Mehmed II.
overview: Ottoman forces under Sultan Mehmed II captured Constantinople after a major siege in 1453.
significance: The fall of Constantinople ended the Byzantine Empire and marked a major transition between the medieval and early modern periods.

timeline.description: The Ottoman siege of Constantinople intensified.
Ottoman forces launched the final assault on the city.
Constantinople fell to the Ottoman army.
